This project uses [Convex](https://convex.dev) as its backend.

When working on Convex code, **always read
`convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first** for important guidelines on
how to correctly use Convex APIs and patterns. The file contains rules that
override what you may have learned about Convex from training data.

Convex agent skills for common tasks can be installed by running
`npx convex ai-files install`.

## Ground every backend and auth change in the skills

This project is mid-migration from Supabase to **Convex + Clerk**. Do not work
from recalled API knowledge for either — both have changed in ways that
training data gets wrong, and we have already lost hours to exactly that.

**Backend / database / Convex functions** → invoke the `convex` skill (it routes
to `convex-quickstart`, `convex-setup-auth`, `convex-migration-helper`,
`convex-performance-audit`, `convex-create-component`), and read
`convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` before writing Convex code.

**Anything auth** → invoke the `clerk` skill (routes to `clerk-nextjs-patterns`,
`clerk-custom-ui`, `clerk-webhooks`, `clerk-backend-api`, `clerk-cli`, …).
Check the installed package version first: `@clerk/nextjs` v7 uses the "future"
hook API (`{ signIn, errors, fetchStatus }`), which is incompatible with the
Core 2 API most examples show.

When a skill and your recollection disagree, the skill wins. When neither
covers the case, **verify against the installed types in `node_modules` or by
logging real runtime values** — do not infer. Inferring is what caused every
bug listed below.

## Hard-won gotchas (all cost real debugging time)

- **Never create a `convex` JWT template in Clerk.** The Convex integration
  (`dashboard.clerk.com/apps/setup/convex`) adds `aud: "convex"` to the default
  session token. `ConvexProviderWithClerk` branches on that claim; a hand-made
  template forces a legacy path and silently drops claims.
- **Clerk config is per-instance.** Development and Production are configured
  separately. A setting applied to one looks successful while changing nothing
  for the other.
- **Clerk's session token is minimal** — `sub`, `sid`, `iss`, `aud`, `sts`, `v`.
  `email` and `name` are present only because we added them via session-token
  customization, on both instances.
- **Auth failures are silent in both directions.** `ConvexProviderWithClerk`
  swallows token errors (`catch { return null }`), and `AuthContext` catches
  mutation errors to `console.error`. Use `npx convex logs` — it is the only
  place failures actually surface.
- **After changing Clerk auth config, sign out and back in.** Cached session
  tokens keep the old claims and reproduce the original symptom.
- **Deploy Convex functions before the frontend.** Convex validates arguments
  strictly; a client that ships first calls validators that reject its args.
- **Never use `.collect().length` to count** and prefer `.take()`/`paginate()`
  over `.collect()` — both are explicit rules in the Convex guidelines.
- **Authorization lives in Convex function bodies**, not middleware. Convex has
  no RLS. `proxy.ts` route matching is a UX affordance only.
